title: How Much Does It Cost to Refinish Hardwood Stairs in Snohomish?
meta: Refinishing hardwood stairs in Snohomish costs $55 to $75 per tread at Wills Flooring. See what sets the per-tread price and price a full 13-step flight here.
keywords: cost to refinish hardwood stairs Snohomish, refinish stairs price per tread, sand and refinish staircase WA, hardwood stair refinishing cost 2027, refinish stair treads Snohomish County

blocks.lead: Wills Flooring refinishes hardwood stairs in Snohomish for $55 to $75 per tread, so a standard 13-step flight runs $715 to $975 on top of the floor it connects to.
blocks.detail: Closed, straight treads sit at the low end. Open-sided treads, pie-shaped winders and stairs with balusters sit at the top. Most Snohomish stair jobs are booked together with the main floor, which is billed at $3.99 per sq ft for a natural finish with a 500 sq ft minimum.

blocks.html: Stairs are the part of a refinishing quote that surprises people. A Snohomish farmhouse with 800 sq ft of fir on the main floor and a steep flight of 14 treads will see nearly a thousand dollars of the quote attached to those steps. That is not padding. Every tread is sanded by hand, the nosing is shaped, the corners are scraped, and each coat is brushed on one step at a time. Here is what you are paying for, what pushes a step from $55 to $75, and when the stairs are not worth refinishing at all.

blocks.text: What a stair tread actually costs to refinish

items.title: Simple tread
items.text: Walls on both sides, a square nosing and painted risers. The edger does most of the work and the coats go on fast. Most 1990s Clearview and Fobes Hill staircases are this type.

items.title: Complex tread
items.text: A returned nosing on an open side, pie-shaped winders around a turn, or a row of spindles that has to be worked around by hand. Old Snohomish Victorians near downtown usually land here.

items.tag: Stained to match a stained floor
items.title: Stained tread
items.text: Stain on stairs means a water-pop, a stain coat wiped by hand, overnight dry time and then the clear coats. Expect the $75 end and an extra day.

blocks.note: Per-tread pricing covers the tread and the exposed nosing. Painted risers are left alone. Wood risers that you want sanded and clear-coated are counted at the estimate.

blocks.text: Why Snohomish stairs cost more per square foot than the floor

items.title: No big machine fits
items.text: A drum sander handles 800 sq ft of open floor in an afternoon. On a stair it never leaves the truck. Each tread is sanded with an edger, a detail sander and a scraper in the corners. A tread is about 3 sq ft, yet it takes 20 to 30 minutes of hand work per grit.

items.title: Three coats, one step at a time
items.text: The floor gets rolled. Stairs get brushed, and every coat has to be applied so nobody walks it wet. On a single-stair house that means the family sleeps downstairs or we finish every other tread over two rounds.

items.title: Old Snohomish stairs hide surprises
items.text: Steep 1900s flights on Avenue D and around Blackmans Lake often have fir treads worn into a dip at the center, cracked nosings and decades of paint on the stringers. A dipped tread can be sanded flat only so far before it gets thin.

items.title: Mud, dogs and boots
items.text: Stairs off a Snohomish mudroom take more abuse than any other wood in the house. We recommend a satin finish and often a fourth coat on the top three treads, which we price on site.

blocks.text: What is under the carpet on your stairs?

blocks.html: Half of the stair calls we get from Snohomish start with "I pulled up the carpet and found wood." Sometimes that wood is a beautiful fir or oak tread. Just as often it is a plywood or particleboard tread that was never meant to be seen. Here is how to tell what you have before you book anything.

blocks.text: When refinishing the stairs is the wrong move

a.title: Worth it when
items: Treads are solid wood with at least 1/8 in above any wear dip
The floor at the top or bottom is being refinished anyway
You want the stairs to match the floor color exactly
Nosings are intact or can be patched

b.title: Skip it when
items: Treads are plywood, particleboard or MDF
Nosings are split along the full length
The stairs are the only wood in the house and you want quiet, soft steps for kids or an older dog
You are re-carpeting the whole upstairs anyway

blocks.title: One honest note on slip:
blocks.text: A freshly finished stair is slicker than carpet, especially in socks. We use a satin sheen on stairs by default, and for Snohomish homes with young kids or big dogs we suggest a low-profile carpet runner installed after the finish cures for a week.
How to keep your stair quote at the low end

items.html: Pull one corner of carpet before we visit. If you can show us a solid tread with a real nosing, the quote is written on the spot. If it is plywood, we save you a wasted appointment.
Paint the risers yourself. Sanded and clear-coated risers add hand work. A painted riser under a natural tread is the look most Snohomish buyers expect anyway.
Do the floor and stairs together. One mobilization, one finish batch, one color. Stairs-only jobs are possible but less efficient, so bundling always wins on price.
Book a dry week if you can. Water-based finish cures faster when the house is not at 70 percent humidity. Winter jobs with the wood stove running are fine; we adjust coat timing.

Ask who is sanding the stairs. Stairs are the hardest part of the job to do well. At Wills Flooring the same Bona Certified Craftsman who does the floor does the treads, and every step is covered by our 1-year workmanship warranty.

faq.q: How much does it cost to refinish 13 stairs in Snohomish?
faq.a: At Wills Flooring's published rate of $55 to $75 per tread, a 13-step flight costs $715 to $975. Closed, straight treads with painted risers land near $715. Open-sided treads, winders or a stain to match the floor push the flight toward $975.

faq.q: Can I refinish only the stairs and not the floor?
faq.a: Yes. Stairs-only jobs happen when a hallway was carpeted and only the stairs are wood. Because there is no square footage to apply the 500 sq ft floor minimum to, we quote stairs-only work at the free estimate so the mobilization is priced fairly.

faq.q: How long does it take to refinish a staircase?
faq.a: One to two days for the sanding and three coats, plus cure time. Because you cannot walk on wet finish, we either coat every other tread in two rounds or coat the whole flight in the evening so it is walkable by morning. Stain adds a day.

faq.q: Do you refinish the risers too?
faq.a: Only if you ask. Most Snohomish stairs have painted risers, and we leave them alone or tape them off. Wood risers you want sanded and clear-coated are counted separately at the estimate because they are done entirely by hand.

faq.q: My stair treads are worn into a dip. Can sanding fix that?
faq.a: Sometimes. Shallow wear sands flat with a few extra passes. If the dip is deep enough that flattening would leave less than about 1/8 in of wood over the nosing, we recommend replacing that tread. We measure each one at the estimate and tell you which are borderline.

Slightly more than carpet, about the same as any hardwood floor. We use a satin sheen rather than gloss on stairs. If you have toddlers or an older dog, a runner installed after the finish has cured for a week is the safest option and it protects the top treads from wear.
